scope_note: Selected decisions relevant to this shard; no blanket re-ratification of the ADRs.

decisions.topic: EC3 numbering of Link versus Ruby/Warichu
decisions.review: The erratum inserts Link as §14.8.4.7.3 and moves existing Ruby/Warichu text to §14.8.4.7.4. Current ledger and tests use the effective number. The child-sequence wording remains unchanged.
decisions.disposition: Retain the numbering correction and audit Ruby/Warichu against unchanged Table 369 text.

decisions.topic: Accessibility representation of structure attributes and Ruby roles
decisions.review: Its assertion that RB's Ruby and RT's RubyAnnotation cross disagrees with current code. `role.rs` maps Ruby→Role::Ruby, RT→Role::RubyAnnotation, RB→Label; AccessKit 0.24.1 / AT-SPI adapter comments describe RubyAnnotation as an annotation node that may appear under Ruby. Existing accessibility tests do not pin the composed hierarchy. The attribute/layout decision for RubyAlign and RubyPosition remains a separate non-implemented layout limitation.
decisions.disposition: Keep the stated layout-attribute boundary, but correct the stale role wording and add a consumer test for a valid Ruby assembly.

decisions.topic: Writer-side scope of file conformance obligations
decisions.review: Its principle applies: Table L.2 binds conforming output produced here. It does not imply that the reading path must reject every source file that violates a producer MUST.
decisions.disposition: Retain, qualified by the narrow generated writer cases this shard inspected.

decisions.topic: One PDF 2.0 Document wrapper when multiple source Documents merge
decisions.review: The implementation and integration test establish one generated root→Document→Document relationship, including a custom role-mapped source case and a default-namespace positive control. This is one Table L.2 case, not a matrix validator.
decisions.disposition: Retain; avoid describing the targeted tests as certification of all Table L.2 relations.

decisions.topic: Derived writer behavior versus carrying source structure
decisions.review: These decisions explain why source elements are not generally rewritten or rejected during carry. A source-invalid relationship can persist without establishing that the reader is obliged to repair it; a newly constructed wrapper still has to be valid.
decisions.disposition: Retain this boundary and report only generated-relationship evidence.

decisions.review: The current notes path reports namespaces that cannot be role mapped and MathML `math` without Formula context. Effective EC3 changed the MathML version reference and enclosure sentence; code comments/test names correctly distinguish this from the older text. The second namespace requirement remains a writer-side vocabulary rule the project declines to enforce without a defined vocabulary inventory.
decisions.disposition: Retain the narrow diagnostic policy and producer-versus-reader distinction; do not call the tests a MathML Core validator.
